messages.subject: spatial dependence model in PRESENCE Question
parts:
Hi fellow Unmarkers,

I have a question in regards of the spatial dependence model that can be run in PRESENCE (Hines et al., 2010) for both single-season and two-species models. I would have posted this question on the online forum for Presence and Mark Programs, both something is going on with their online registration at the moment. Anyways....

I am using presence/absence data along with data for a few different covariates at different spatial scales to answer questions in regards to the occurrence of a rare species of stream fish. Four spatially replicated surveys (Sur_1, Sur_2, etc) were performed to produce our detection histories, and data for 6 occupancy covariates and 3 sampling covariates were also collected. Occupancy covariates were associated with either the site scale (depth (SD), velocity (SV), woody debris (WD), substrate), or the watershed scale (stream link magnitude and %Forest cover). Sampling covariates included:  mean velocity, mean depth, and mean substrate for each spatial replicate within the site. I constructed 4  models in PRESENCE using these data and the spatial dependence model. I also constructed 4 models with the same model design (i.e., models contained exactly the same covariates), but instead were run with the single-species, single season model (as this model assumes independence among surveys). The objective was to determine which model type (spatial dependence, or simple single season) provided a better explanation of the observed data, based on AIC ranking. 

Constructed models (for both the spatial dependence and simple season models) would look something like this, using the occu formulation in R

1. (~Velocity+Depth+Substrate~SV)
 
2. (~Velocity+Depth+Substrate~SD)

3.  (~Velocity+Depth+Substrate~LINK)

4. (~Velocity+Depth+Substrate~LINK + Forested)




Interestingly, models constructed with just the site scale-occupancy variables did not detect spatial autocorrelation (which is what I would have suspected). The models constructed with ONLY occupancy covariates at the watershed scale; however, did detect spatial autocorrrelation (as the spatial dependence version of these models were ranked higher than their simple single season counterparts) in the detection histories. My question is: why am I seeing spatial autocorrelation in the models using only the watershed scale covariates and not in the models constructed with the site scale covariates? This is very confusing!  If anyone can help me answer this conundrum it would be much appreciated!

I have attached the data if anyone wants to take a crack at it in PRESENCE,  using the models above. 


Regards,

Josh
